Were you prepared for the greatest battle this world had ever seen?

You only had a small chance, but the most skilled and ambitious sorcerers of this world joined you... Klavdia, Catherina, and Zayan...

It is time... I will tell you the words of those who were about to witness the Battle of Gods:

"The Gates are about to let one mighty enemy into our world, and the Seals can barely contain the rage of the other one... I'm ashamed to say that, but I'm afraid. Very afraid! The greatest battle in history is going to unfold before our eyes, and I'm trembling like a village girl at the sight of a soldier.

I'm sure my plan will work, but we can't afford to make a single mistake. The gods have to destroy each other. If one of them wins, it will be the end of everything that you know and love.  It will be the end of me. So there will be no winners in this battle!" said Klavdia.

"I don't like this idea... But since I can't stop you, I'll do my best to help you, though I can't let you destroy the world right now.

I swore to repay my old debt, and I will. Nobody knows how to control the flow of pure energy better than I do, because as soon as you break a Seal, it will flood the whole place with energy. I will distribute it between our sorceresses so they can prevent either of the gods from winning. They will also protect us if necessary. And you... Cut, slice, burn - do whatever it takes to stop the gods from getting the upper hand!

Interfering in gods' affairs is dangerous, bid it's even more dangerous to sit idle when the fate of the world is at stake! After the Seals are destroyed, the biggest battle in the history of Sarnaut will begin! I will not ask whether you are ready for that - nobody is. Just let me know when we can start.

It will be a dreadful battle... If there's a winner, the rest of us will die, and that's why there will be no winners! None! The gods have to fall... at any cost!

We just had to split our forces between Sarn and the Architect:

"Daddy always said I was Chaos incarnate... We'll see if it's true! The Architect is mine! Catherina, attack Sarn!" said Klavdia.

"She's giving me orders, huh! I was going to make him pay for Umoir anyway!" smirked Catherina.
text

The Dead City again. How many years has it been since that battle? That's what Klavdia said:

"My father created the Star Gates for his own purposes only. Even I can't bypass the powerful spells that are to designed to kill anyone who tries to travel between the worlds.

I'm sure that, with your assistance, I will be able to weaken their defense, but be ready to fight. Fight what? I have no idea what we might face, but I know my father loves surprises. So be ready for anything! You might even have to fight upside down!"

As soon as you used the Key and opened the Star Gates, an unusual dragon emerged - the guard placed here by Nihaz.

"The Gates are open; the Seal is broken, but there is a small problem. There it is, above our heads. If I'm right, and I'm always right, it's called the Void Dragon. It doesn't belong to our world, and I'm afraid I don't know anything about its weaknesses. All I can do is change gravity so you can battle the beast at close range, but that's about it. It's taking all my strength to keep the Gates from closing," said Klavdia.

The battle ended in the monster's death, even though the power of gravity was on its side.

"Phew! The Void Dragon... I didn't think anyone could make this creature serve them. I heard these Dragons live in the Void between the worlds. The Great Dragons who guard Sarn's prison were created in their image. I hope there will be no more surprises like this. I don't think you want to be a star in the literal sense."
text

Oh, the Wormface champion. Did you know they have three castes? Warriors, Psionicists, and Mages? The Destroyers are sort of a caste within a caste, elite warriors.

This is what Klavdia said:

Behind these gates is the temple of the most powerful Wormface warriors who call themselves the Destroyers. They are mighty enemies, and the power of the Seal Shard makes them deadly. You shouldn't face them on your own. Join a raid, and maybe you will make it out of the sanctuary alive!"

Alright, you entered the temple. There was someone waiting to greet you:

"Only the strongest of the strongest are allowed to touch the Shrine!

So you come from the surface... We've been watching you.

You wish to touch our Shrine? Learn the secrets of the Origins? Well, since you're here, you probably know how it's done. The only question is, are you worthy?"

Teumim fought bravely, but you defeated him.

So what is the Bestiary?

The Empire's secret training ground where they performed experiments on various local animals. The key part of these experiments was an object that was found in that very lake, enclosed in a piece of a meteorite. The Imperials used it on test subjects with varying degrees of success. As you can see, that worm, the "Specimen", managed to escape in the end. It settled somewhere around here.

Meanwhile, the local animals started to suffer from some kind of disease. They began to turn into "modificants". Do you remember the Blight? Wait, it's not that simple!

I'll remind you about something else - on the Eclipse, when you fought Captain Krivov, his construct turned into some kind of creature that emanated the air of "order", right? Does anything here seem familiar to you?

Okay, let’s get back to business. Finding an entrance to the Bestiary was not easy. You were lucky. This is how Herbert put it:

"One of our jaegers, Sergey Dozorin, sent me a message yesterday. He has found another entrance to the Bestiary. He has somehow activated a Portal in a cave in the Deadly Frostland. The Tungars use that cave it for their pagan rituals. And we have both seen what Tungar gods are capable of...

I don't think you will be able to get past them undetected like Dozorin did, but you can always fight your way through. Maas-Tyna the Light-Footed in our first camp can show you the way.

The Bestiary might have answers to many of our questions, so we can't miss this opportunity to find them."

Did this piece of rock really cause all the problems on Ferris? Strange mutations, security systems going haywire, dead scientists - all because of a small piece of crystal matter? Unbelievable...

We should ask the Surveyors about the crystal and the energy it's emitting. Maybe together we will solve this riddle!

You spoke with Elena Zimina first:

"You think this crystal caused the mutation? Hmm... I find that hard to believe. Those mutations are random - no two cases are alike, so I think it would be more accurate to call it modification - making deliberate changes to living organisms in order to produce a desired result - rather than mutation.

I think you should speak with Herbert. He knows more about these things."
text

Herbert was skeptical:

"A crystal as a source of mutation? That's not possible!

Yes, I can sense that it radiates some energy, but I don't understand its nature. If it's magic, then it's really unusual. But I have no doubt that this crystal was extracted from the meteorite at the bottom of the lake and transported to the Bestiary. What does that tell us? Two things!

First, the crystal was the key element of the scientists' research. Perhaps constant exposure to its radiation caused unexpected results.

Second, we don't know whether the experiment was successful or not. The Bestiary was abandoned a long time ago, and we don't know if the mutation was created on purpose or it was a side effect.

You know... I think you should speak with someone who knows more about technology and magic than anyone else in Sarnaut. Besides, they owe you their life. Can you guess who they are? The Great Sorceress Catherina!
text

Well, I guess it's time to go back to Umoir and talk to our old acquaintance:

"What brings you to my chambers? Are you here to boast about your triumph and gloat over my failure?

Where did you get this crystal?! Give it to me, I must... Oh, sorry! I'm still a little out of it after the whole Blight business.

Yes, I know something about this crystal. Long ago, I saw a shard like this one. It was about the size of my pinkie. The man who gave it to me said he'd found it on a wrecked ship covered in dead bodies of the Zem. I suppose those were Tep's followers - the Arisen who believed in the Light would have resurrected after death.

My research showed that the stone was emitting an unidentified energy. Its power was so strong that it suppressed and altered all other known magical fields. I tried but couldn't find a use for it, so in the end it became a part of the battery backup circuit for one of my mechanism. That device is still on the Eclipse... Oh, wait, you destroyed it when you were fighting my loyal captain Krivov!

I'm sorry, there is nothing else I can do. Captain Krivov is dead, and all my scientific research has turned to a pile of scrap metal, all thanks to you. No, no, I'm not blaming you - back then I wasn't myself. I didn't know what I was doing when I brought the world to the brink of destruction. But I can't help you now either.

If you don't mind, I will keep the shard and continue my research. If this is how it affects both living flesh and metal, I need to find a way to use it to battle the Blight. What if it's our only chance?!"
text

As I said, more and more altered creatures were waiting for you. I still marvel at the carelessness of the Imperial scientists. In their pursuit of scientific discovery, they were willing to perform the most irresponsible and risky experiments. The League's Catherina is the same. So you can't help but wonder - is it the gods that are a threat to the world? Or is it us?

This is what the jaeger said:

"Remember how the Tungars were scared of yaks? Taming and driving the poor animal mad is the greatest feat for them. I'd like to see how they deal with an experimental specimen from the Bestiary. Yes, yes. Our precursors experimented even on yaks!

I managed to get into the archives of the Bestiary and found something about the research that was conducted in the year of the incident. The documents are surprisingly well-preserved and, most importantly, sorted into categories. Meet your enemy - the Thunderer project. It's an attempt to turn a yak into an energy-producing machine. According to the documents, the attempt failed. But I've seen the yak with my own eyes just recently. Even in the turbulent sectors of the Astral, I've never seen so many lightning bolts that illuminated the area around the creature. That's energy, isn't it?

I think that the mutation somehow affected its abilities.

I wonder if the mutation was accidental, or those scientists actually found a way to engineer it. Anyway, we will have to kill the monster before it becomes too dangerous."

Victory! Why are you surprised? Did you want to keep going?

"I wonder if one can dodge a lightning bolt. Can you try? Please?

"Well... That Thunderer is an interesting individual for sure. My ears are still ringing!

We are on the right track. Baxter refuses to keep moving, and he's a smart dog, if timid. And I can feel that we're close to the source of the mysterious disease."
text

Ferris has all sorts of creatures on it. Like the Gastornis, those overgrown chickens...

Let's hear what Sergey Dozorin had to say:

"Alright, here is the deal.

They say there is a rooster in every yard in Kanian villages. To wake them up in the morning, or to keep hens happy - I'm not sure. The Bestiary has its rooster, too. It's a Gastornis, actually. A giant bird that can only be found on Ferris. It can't fly - I bet that's why it's so angry. If you live right next to creatures with a taste for bird meat, there's only one thing you can do - become the scariest beast in the neighborhood and eat everyone yourself.

Our rooster learned that lesson well. So it will try to eat you as soon as it sees you. Just because it can. You will be intruding into its territory, after all. Unfortunately, there is no way you can get around it. It picked a perfect spot.

The good news is, this specimen is the only one of its kind. A relict creature, as the Surveyors call it. If you deal with it, you won't have to worry about Gastornises ever again."

There you have it. Did you deal with it? Can some bird stop the Hero of Sarnaut? Exactly, and don't you doubt it.

"That chicken was stronger than I thought! How are you? Are you alright? Still have all your limbs? Great. Now let's explore the Bestiary."
text

Ooh, we're getting close to the source of all evil. You've already rescued Zimina from that creature - now you need to save the entire Ferris.

I'll repeat what Sergey Dozorin said:

"You know, I remember what you told me about your vision... And I've come to realize that you saw the heart of the mutation. Though you probably don't remember that.

There is a dead zone in the far end of the Bestiary. Animals and birds keep away from it. My dog refuses to go there, and honestly, I don't really want to myself. But I don't have a choice...

There must be a cave deep inside the complex. Whatever is in there, it holds answers to our questions. You will have to fight the thing that has destroyed the whole Bestiary. I've already called the technicians of the expedition - they are bringing all the necessary gear: hovering platforms, turrets, explosives... So you will also have to keep the staff and the equipment safe!

But don't be sad. Responsibility means trust, right? Just try not to die in there, alright? I'm sure we will need you help in the future. Good luck!"

Yes! That icy worm is dead! The story of the Bestiary would have ended there, but an unexpected discovery shed light on an old mystery.

"A crystal? A single stone drove all the animals in the area mad and turned them into monsters? Damn...

Well, I will leave this mystery to someone else. Baxter and I have better things to do. I'll go find the Prowls. I could do with a cup of their famous brew.

You really are good! I've heard a lot about you. But you know how people are - you can't believe everything you hear. Now I'm wondering who should be feared more, those defeated monsters... or you? Hmm.

Never mind.  It's time for a drink!

"So, our ways are parting. You need to go with the expedition, and I'm staying in the Bestiary. It's more peaceful here. And just I like the place, you know.

The most interesting things must be waiting for you in the heart of Ferris! Stick with Herbert. He is a smart and capable guy. You can rely on him in any situation!" said the brave hunter and bid you farewell. Now you need to show the crystal to the Surveyors.
text

Well, you took your first steps inside the Bestiary. The real surprises were still waiting for you. What's important is how the local fauna was changing...

It's not the first time it has occurred. Of course, it never happened on Sarnaut. A certain mind was behind these changes. A mind that was obsessed with order. Absolute, perfect order.

And there was an unusual kitty waiting for you...

"How much do you rely on your eyes? Jaegers are taught that your ears and nose are as important as your eyes. I still need Baxter to sniff things out for me, because the human sense of smell isn't nearly as strong. No, don't whine, buddy! Ah, this dog is too smart...

Alright. The deeper we go, the worse it gets. All animals inside the Bestiary seem to be covered with some sort of stone crust. Many of them are already dead, but the survivors... have turned into real monsters. Take that huge cougar. It keeps prowling around the complex and sniffing the air. A strange behavior, isn't it? That's what I thought so I decided to observe it quietly. And I realized that it had gone completely blind because of the mutation, so it relies on its hearing and sense of smell. You think it makes it weaker? Oh, no. It sees with its ears and nose just fine! And it's a problem for us! I barely managed to trick it so it couldn't hear me as I ran away.

But we can't keep tricking it forever. If you want to get deeper into the complex, you need to deal with it first. Or else we'd be ambushed at the most inopportune moment."

That's what we deal with here. There'll be more of them up ahead. Even if Rustle couldn't stop you, you still need to be careful.

You can't really sneak up on this creature. This creature can hear even the slightest movement...

As the Pridens say, that was one fine hunt! You can be proud of yourself - this was not just a fight with a huge cat. It's a proof that mutated animals can be killed. And that's great! Now we know that we can gain control over the Bestiary and unravel its secrets."

So what's the conclusion? Herbert discovered some sort of artifact in a protective sarcophagus. Opening it took a while, so the Surveyors decided to take the time to explore the numerous halls of the complex. Some of them lead to a valley hidden from everyone.

Herbert decided to deal with Negus Jeeg who apparently played a key role in the fate of this Laboratory.

But before we could get to this mad Zem, we had to deal with the Mechanoid sentries and Herbert's clone.

On Jeeg's body you found a journal. This diary helped us bring Tep's story to a close - the reason you came to Ferris in the first place:

Negus Jeeg's Journal.

The journal is written in a weird language. Must be an ancient one.

...That's an interesting book! It looks like Negus Jeeg wrote these notes - they are all in Hickut. Semer Hatshah can translate them. What if it's something important?

"Hickut, you say? Let me see... Oh, it is indeed. Finally something for me to do. Anything will do around here. Which parts do we need? Give me a couple of minutes, I will translate it."

Negus Jeeg's notes about being appointed as the Head of the Research Complex.

January 11, 964

"The sudden death of Vasily Dankin has led to my appointment as the Head of the Research Complex. My little scheme worked better than I'd hoped. Now the staff are all pawns in my hands... and in Tep's hands. Soon their Sparks will follow Dankin. Soon. But not now. For now, I need them."

…

March 26, 964

A Council agent has arrived to Ferris to supervise the development of the new ship prototype. I had no choice but to demonstrate the efficiency of the experimental ship reactor... Too bad he won't be able to tell anyone about it - there's just a handful of dust left of him. The Empire will have to do without new ships. Tep does not want the League to fall... I have sent the schematics of experimental Mechanoids to my associates."

…

September 3, 964

"The research of the Object is going well. It holds more mysteries than the Great Mages... and even Tep himself could have imagined in their wildest dreams. Beyond all doubt, this is a source of a great power. I'm finally on the right track."
text

December 4, 965

...this entry ends abruptly. Something must have happened while it was being written.

The adepts tried to get inside my head, but much to my surprise, they couldn't. They just couldn't. It puzzled them (and me). I'm writing this in my room - they placed me "under house arrest". The cult won't help me. We are too weak. I guess I will hav..."

…

January 14, 966

"I don't remember the last month. Since the last entry, things have been foggy. Today I woke up in the middle of an empty corridor, surrounded by my former colleagues. Those blue eyes and the ringing silence. It didn't disturb me at all. I was calm. But what has happened in the last month?"

…

January 15, 966

"The Mechanoids are collecting the dead bodies all over the complex and throwing them into the Astral. Is that how they get rid of the evidence? Wrecked Astral ships are floating around the allod - so they did try to escape... Idiots. For now, I haven't come across a single living (sentient) being in the entire facility. But I've seen Nezeb's stamp on a document in my office. The Council has shut down the whole research. This complex no longer exists. It's a ghost complex. And I'm its only inhabitant."
text

October 5, 966

"I hear Nezeb died. I don't know where I heard that. But I know that. That's amusing. I'd uncork a bottle of champagne, but it's bad for my prostheses. I gave it to one of the blue-eyed. I think he liked it. I taught him to say "Glory to Tep!" Now he wanders around, mumbling it.

…

Some summer month. 973.

"He is silent. Everybody is silent. I'm alone. It's a nice day."

…

New Year's Eve, 977.

"The animals who call themselves Pridens just broke in. They babbled something about some Shoom branch and poked the Mechanoids with their hammers and sticks. Luckily, I had switched them off long ago. Now I have someone to talk to."

…

January 14, 978 (that's what the furry ones say)

I don't understand half of what they're saying, but I like them (especially their cloaks!). The blue-eyed don't seem to notice them. Which means the Object doesn't care about their presence. I have an idea."

…

June 2, 978

"Well, Tep can be proud of me. The tribe has left, determined to wipe out their home allod. I never knew I was so good at public speeches. Or was it the champagne? Ah, no... I've run out of it long ago."

…

Idontcarewhatdayitis, 986

"Perfection. I've achieved it. Peace is next. I've got nothing to eat, so I don't. It is easier than it seems - the blue-eyed know that."

…

Lost track of time. Need to find out what day it is.

I've cloned a deer. Just for laughs. And food, of course. The blue-eyed taste bad, the wires especially."
text

January 1, 1000

"I hear exited voices coming from somewhere. The new millennia. The first day. Oh, this is so important.  I'm making an entry just to mark that. I should keep track of time. Tick-tock. It's so slow. I can keep up with it, even on my rusty prostheses. I think Tep was supposed to come in the past millennia. Or the next one? I don't remember."

…

June 5, 1010

"Here he is. Speak of the devil, hahahahaha!! He's been lying in the coffin for ages... I asked if he wanted to shower - we have a bathroom in the back. He looked at me like I was an idiot. That damned egghead. And his Mechanoids are ugly, though they were based on my schematics. And he himself looks... wrong. The Source is more beautiful. The Source told me that Tep is just a drop in the ocean. That Tep is useless. I should kick Tep out. He has no business being here. Get out!"

…

 "Everything is smoking and shaking! I think Tep is angry. I never thought he could scream like that. For a moment, I was genuinely afraid. Maybe he was practicing? I need to practice, too (will start tomorrow after lunch). The bad news is that the Source wasn't able to resist him. If it hadn't been for my Mechanoids, I'd be dead right now. So what should you say? Thank you, Negus Jeeg. It's a good thing you exist."

After reading the journal, Herbert realized a few things:

"Well... the pieces finally fall into place. Negus Jeeg was Tep's cultist who was in charge of the whole complex. That's quite an undertaking... But what happened next? How did that "Object" make him turn against his master? What is "perfection"? What is the Source?

Whatever the answers to these questions are, we probably won't like them. I'm starting to wonder if it might be better for us to forget about Ferris, like the Empire did once."
text

As you can see, the Mechanoids were originally created by this psychopath. He's quite a skilled one. Lots of the things he created are still operational to this day. But his most successful invention is the security system of the Central Laboratory. And now it has also been "modified" and upgraded!

This is what Herbert said:

"As you already know, this place is mostly guarded by the Mechanoids. They do it pretty well - the scientists are long gone, and they are still protecting the complex! But what if the Mechanoids had been affected by the "modifying crystal" back then? Would they have continued following the orders, or would they have turned against their owners? It's a tricky question, and we will have to answer it.

Modified Mechanoids that guard the laboratory are blocking our way. I have no idea what they are capable of. This technology is far more advanced than anything the Elves or the ZIT Headquarters could have come up with. I wish we didn't have to destroy it.

Come back as soon as you're done with them. We'll decide what to do next.

The design of the robots suggests they were meant to operate in pairs. Though occasionally they fire on each other."

You managed to defeat the machines.

"Alas, even the most advanced technology is inferior to the destructive genius of vanda... great heroes, I mean. I will ask our technicians to find out as much as possible about these Mechanoids. There may be many more mechanical modificants out there that we'll have to deal with eventually. I will keep you informed.

Enough talking. Let's get to work.
text

"I want to play a game with you..."

Oh, that Negus Jeeg of yours is a terrifying one. I've never liked madmen, but this Arisen is something else.

What can one say about a maniac's motives? You never know what's going on in their head. That's why they are so dangerous.

Herbert understood that as well as I do.

"Well... Now I can see all the sections of the complex. The damned maniac who has created the clones knows that, and sooner or later he will try to take control. We can't waste time! We need to kill him now! There are so many rat holes he can use in this laboratory.

I will show you the way... Hurry, before he strikes! Be careful - we don't know what to expect from him. There is nothing more dangerous than a mad fanatic! He's been surviving here on his own all this time. I wonder how...

He might want to play one of his nasty games with you. Be on your guard!"

I hope it was the real Jeeg you took down. That it was the original, and not a copy. That this maniac is not hiding somewhere in the complex...

"Dead? Oh... I know, one shouldn't rejoice at someone's death, but I'm still glad you put an end to his wretched existence.

We've already started digging through the laboratory's archives. The madman's name was Negus Jeeg - he used to be the head of the complex. He took the position after his predecessor died in the "incident" in the Bestiary. You probably remember it.

I feel like we don't have a complete picture..." concluded the leader of the Surveyors.

The City of Demons...

The atrium of Gorluxor's Tower and the most sinister place in Sarnaut at this time. Why would you want to go there? Let me remind you.

So it all started with the events in the Holy Land, when the cultists led by Gorluxor, the rebellious Great Mage from the Empire, tried to destroy the Gift of Tensess. Or rather, their goal was to claim this Gift for the demons. You managed to thwart their plans.

But it turned out that the world the League and the Empire had believed in for the last fifty years was false. The demons were not defeated at the June Gates during the Great Astral Campaign. They are still active, and they are trying to destroy the allods.

The realization brought you all here. You rightly believe that Gorluxor and his cultists are behind everything. That's why you are now standing here at the Gates of this City.

After working out a truce, the League and Empire are about to storm it. Are you ready to join the attack? Or do you want to know what happened next?
text

Armando de Doucer. A Vampire Knight, traitor to the Elves. The Patriarch of the House de Doucer.

You must have heard of him. But the people of the League know him best.

Let me remind you: he's a leader of one of the Great Elven Houses who violated the rules of the Great Game. During a Great Ball, he put a deadly curse on the bride of the man he lost to. When his actions were discovered, Armando and his House were exiled.

They dreamed of revenge, and Tep came to their aid. He granted Armando powers of astral darkness, and soon almost the entire House de Doucer turned into vampires. Armando once again intervened in the next Great Ball, capturing the Galleon Castle of the House de Ardeur and turning it into Darkblood Citadel. That's where justice was dispensed - by order of the Tenebran governor, Marguerite de Desirae, the heroes of the League cut off Armando's head.

You might remember that a severed head makes resurrection impossible. The spark cannot return to the body if it's missing the head. But as it turned out, Armando managed to get around it. You met him on Avilon, in another Galleon Castle which was created by Gorluxor this time. Armando boasted of his resurrection but was killed again.

And now you need to end his life again. For the last time. But the mystery of his resurrection remains unsolved for the time being.

Armando won't be alone - his inner circle will be with him. After leaving his wife Carmilla on Umoir, the Patriarch is ready to fight for Gorluxor and keep you from going any further. But it won't help him. You will win this time, too.
text

Kazul the Astral Watcher. Gorluxor's Watchman. You crossed the quarters of the City of Demons and entered the Tower. Here, each step takes tremendous effort. Every step is a fallen cultist, demon, troll, or Searing Eye.

But the real challenge is still ahead. When he was still an Imperial Great Mage, Gorluxor experimented on living beings, trying to change them using special technology. Here, in the Tower he had rebuilt to his liking, he continued his experiments. The result is a powerful Searing Eye, a many-eyed watchman who does not let anyone get close to his master.

But it won't be an obstacle to you.
text

Excellent. So you decided to go in. But surely you didn't expect it to be easy? It wasn't. The City of Demons is divided into quarters cleverly connected by demonic portals. With the help of your Great Mages, Aidenus and Yasker, you learned how to hack them. You move forward, stepping over the bodies of those madmen who crave the destruction of the world. Who leads them? You can only guess.

As you already know, this demonic cult is an example of a complex hierarchy. But even a cult needs those who will just stand guard. At the start, it is Gog and Magog, two trolls clad in armor. After slaying them, you stop in front of a cup of blood. Use the blood of the cultist you killed and draw the attention of the real threat - the dead ogre Nogrom.

Demons and necromancy? We will talk about this later. The ogre is powerful, and the blows of its club will knock you down. But he is nothing to the heroes of Sarnaut. Victory lets you decide where to go next. Old enemies or new ones?
text

Zalmar the Twisted. A demon leader. Don't think demons have gender. It's just a convention that has a symbolic meaning. War'kaz the Mindreaver was brutal, but Zalmar the Twisted is insidious. A skilled mage who channels the power of the Astral, she has killed many.

In the City of Demons, she is tasked with collecting and protecting the mana Gorluxor and his henchmen may need.

Of course, your task was to eliminate her. If you were able to get past her, you could keep going.
text

A voice came from the Abyss.

"I don't recommend jumping into this chasm... The secrets it hides are beyond your understanding... And it will hurt when you fall. Leave. While you still can."

You ignored the strange voice and started descending. Strange cobwebs and unusual demons awaited you. The voice kept talking:

"So stubborn... What am I to do with you...?"

You kept going, through the cobwebs and the demons attacking you.

"You don't understand...  You resist... I've had enough of this!"

It's a strange place that seemingly spawns demons…

"This should stop you!"

As you descend into the Abyss, you run into a strange old man who looks more comical than threatening. The old man was waving a stick and shouting threats:

"Ah! You are forcing me to punish you. You will regret it! On the other hand... Who else would do it? No one, apparently... Well? Ready for your lesson? Let's begin!"

But the funny old man turned out to be extremely powerful. The fight was not easy. Those who had mind powers could hear the fragments of this Master's thoughts:

"You are making a mistake... Do not attempt to infiltrate my mind, fool! You will regret it!"

"I've been imprisoned for millions of years! I can wait a little longer."

"It gives me unbearable pleasure to destroy things I love most!"

"Nihaz... Nihaz... One day I will say this name for the last time!"

"I saw the creation and death of many worlds! You can never hope to challenge me, mortals!"

"Why? Why are you doing this? Go away, I don't want to hurt you. I have already done enough evil..."

"For thousands of years I've been a prisoner in a cage of my own fears... But now... When I have discovered how cunning my enemy is, nothing will stop me!"

"Please go. The innocents shall not suffer anymore. Your deaths will not save this world."

"No, I'm not broken! The years spent in prison tempered my rage! Run, insects, before my hatred burns you to ashes!"

"Well, well, well... You think you're heroes? You are flies caught in a web of delusion! And I will swat you!"

And when he was seemingly defeated, something incredible happened. The old man split into two parts: one was unthinkably beautiful, and the other was disgustingly terrible. A beautiful angel and a disgusting spider, so big that it filled the entire Abyss with its body.

"I will destroy you!" said the Dark Side.

"I will join in!" said the Light Side.

It was a terrible battle. Both the Light and Dark sides wielded immense power. By some miracle, you defeated them.

"Well, this is a victory... Your victory... But let's see what you say when the consequences follow! We will meet again, my children!" the creature said in the end.
text

Strina the Fierce The Lady of Death. Another one you've met before. Of course, only the Imperials know her true story. I'll tell you about it.

The Orcs do not have magic powers that would allow them to become Great Mages and hold their allod. It's a well-known fact. However, for many centuries, there has been a legend about an orc who had magic powers. The shamans did not know his name or where he came from and when he lived, but they started looking for his descendants.

More recently, they managed to get on the trail of these descendants. A family of two brothers and a sister was found. Stormrider, Skulnar, and Strina the Fierce However, when the shamans tried to win them over to their side, tragedies started befalling them. Stormrider was the first to die. Conscripted into the army, he fell during the League's attack on Igsh.

Strina was found next. The Hero of the Empire helped her avoid the problems associated with her gift, but then she refused to help the shamans and decided to choose her own fate after gaining a powerful ally.

Finally, Skulnar - his story is even more heartbreaking. He became a victim of the Empire's experiments. Transformed into a half-machine, he went mad during a diversion created by Tep and was killed during the cleanup of Lab-13.

Strina was found again on Coldberg where she tried to destroy the deposits of meteoric iron with her undead and demonic allies. After becoming a cultist, she became an enemy of this world and was also killed. As you can guess, Gorluxor was the ally she gained.

And now we meet her again. As you understand, death is not an obstacle for Gorluxor's allies, and Strina can ally herself even with Death. You have encountered Nogrom, one of her creations. And she is ready to summon more of those creatures.

The Orcs are not sorcerers, but Strina's gift made her strong enough to contend even with the Great Mages. She is a powerful summoner, which makes her extremely dangerous.
text

War'kaz the Mindreaver A demon commander. He can do everything they can. But better. This demon is focused destruction. Someday you will understand the true meaning of my words, but for now...

The thing is, demons don't have names. Just the nicknames you or the cultists give them. Few can remember this demon. Because few survived an encounter with him. I could tell you about the ships he sank, the allods he burned down.

This astral demon lived in the most fiery sectors of the astral. Now he is called here to protect this city.

Of course, he is extremely dangerous. And, of course, you defeated him.
text

"Right behind me you can see the entrance to the second stage, lit by the crimson flame of the scaly horde of the Draconids and their Fiery Father. They tried to outplay me on my own turf. And they failed. They just don't know it yet, haha.

Finally, behind the third set of gates are the once-great Junes who now resemble a drunkard's nightmare: the Wormfaces led by their relentless leader, Zak. It was his Spark they were able to steal from me on the Isle of Revelation. He has a new body now... But something tells me he's not happy with it.

The best part is that all of them - the Draconids, the Wormfaces, and Sarn's demons - all fear something more than they fear me! They are afraid that someone else will get here first, to the heart of the Dead City. Each of them is trying to reach an agreement with me behind the others' backs, promising to help destroy what they imagine are my enemies. Hah! Just think about it: they all want to settle their scores with their long-time enemies by having someone else do the dirty work!

You can probably guess what brought the Wormfaces, the Draconids, and even the demons here, to the Dead City? Hehe. Look up! See that huge structure? That is the key... and lock in one. But let's leave its purpose a secret for now. You will learn everything in due time. One shouldn't change horses in midstream, right?

Let the play begin!"

So, each of the three enemies of Nihaz dreamed of a prize, something that's in the very center of the Dead City. At first, you didn't understand what exactly you were seeing… Understanding will come later. And now you had to choose which of the enemies of the Dark God will be defeated first.
text

You want to know about your possible future?

Well, surprises await you... But let's start from the beginning. You have joined the Game of the Gods that Dadd... Nihaz and Sarn started. You already know some of the details of their confrontation. But new pieces appeared on this board - the Great Dragon, aka the Fiery Father, and Ath-Zak, the June hero, and they all made their moves.

I'll give the floor to Nihaz:

"Welcome to the Dead City, my trusty helper! Are you still trying to understand the secrets of the world? That's quite commendable! I've already told you that brawn alone won't get you far. It's not enough to be physically strong. You have to know how to apply this strength. And this is why you're here now. The throne room of the Dead City is where everything started, and it's where everything will end... All the figures in our story are already in their places, eager to play their roles in our new play. Three acts on three stages! And you will be playing the lead role. For my part, I'll stay here in the audience.

Look right. Behind this gate is the first stage - the ruins defiled by demons. I'm sure they're just dying to break free and tear everyone in the audience to shreds. It's too bad they're too weak to tussle with a god. No matter what they do, their powers are essentially useless, because the gates open on my command!"
text

Aidenus found out about it and said:

"I see... Not the news I thought I'd hear. Now listen to me. After the catastrophe, people needed a symbol to unite around, and that's what we gave them. Well, twelve symbols. The dead can no longer be saved, but their memories remain with the living. And the power... Does it matter who has it if they use it for good? Power is neutral. But people, sentient beings, are polarized. To be honest, it's nice to have my suspicions confirmed. For now, it's not important which ones. As for the Star Gates, I'm actually pleased to know that they are inaccessible to us.  Imagine what would have happened if we had gotten our hands on them. The Gibberlings would have found themselves a new land. The great Elven houses would have sprung up everywhere, then quickly withered due to lack of challenge and competition. As for the Kanians, they would've lost their roots, forgotten their ancestors and their faith... And what is a people without roots? Dust on the roads of history! It will be better if you don't tell everyone what you've learned..."

Apparently Yasker said the same thing:

"Hmm... I wasn't wrong. This is not good news. But it looks like you did the right thing. The Star Gates... Can you imagine what would have happened if the Empire had taken them? We would have probably succumbed to temptation and set off to conquer new worlds. The Empire would have grown too big and gained too much power. And then? I'm tempted by these lovely visions, but I know what unfettered expansion brings. Believe me, I've seen it, and it's tragic. Now, about the Patrons. And don't tell anyone what you know. Yes. There were no great martyrs. But this is one of the biggest state secrets, one of many that you need to keep to yourself. People needed a symbol to unite around, and that's what we gave them. Well, twelve symbols. The dead can no longer be saved, but their memories remain with the living. You can tell the Keeper of Secrets everything you know, but no one else should know this!"

The Star Gates are still in the Dead City. Now inaccessible, they were useless. Perhaps eventually someone would find a Key that would open them. But it's a completely different story.
text

I will have repeat other people's words again. As you understand, after your meeting with Ath-Zak in Tka-Rik's Cave, he was resurrected. The Wormfaces used the same plans that you were going to use to give Osip a new body. Someone else's body...

I'll warn you just in case: without a properly hardened Spark, it's a disastrous idea. The spark is attached to the body. Trying to shove it into another is like trying to wear clothes that don't fit. It is very, very difficult to comprehend the possibility of rebirth... Ath-Zak was not ready for this.

But I will quote Nihaz and repeat the orders he gave you:

"It's time to end one of the plotlines in our play. Zak is a pain in the neck, frankly speaking. Capricious and ignorant. And yet you all consider him to be some sort of hero? So he defeated a demon, but only just, and he did that with the help of a Great Mage. Pshaw!

Either way, the fools that snatched his Spark consider him something of a deity. They follow him like sheep. Once was not enough for them, apparently. We'll have to teach them another lesson.

Pass through the gates to the Lower City and deal with Zak once and for all. As a Spark he's much more tolerable.

Of course, it wasn't easy to defeat the last of the Junes. But is there anything you can't do?
text

"So Zak is still as chatty as ever?

Right, so I won't have to listen to his babbling for the next few centuries. Ha ha!

Perhaps I'll even move his Spark to a new body after a while... After all, his people almost defeated the dragons, and he alone had enough pride and courage to stand against me. Which means there's still hope for him."

That's the epitaph the last of the Junes got from the Dark God. But he told you something...

"Finally... You have no idea how much I've suffered in this body! Cursed Nihaz... It's all his fault. His lies led my people to a disgraceful end.

You are but a blind pawn in the dark god's game. I'm thankful that you've put an end to my suffering. I'll tell you the real reason that compelled me to challenge Nihaz.

Long ago, when my people were strong, we nearly wiped out the dragons. But then Nihaz appeared and said that if Sarn were to be freed, the universe would be destroyed, along with all of us. Nihaz can be convincing. He showed us the Star Gates, a structure that the gods use to travel between worlds. He promised he would give us a new world where we would reign. When Sarn cursed my people, the survivors ran to Nihaz, begging him to fulfill his promise.

What's interesting is that Nihaz almost never tells a downright lie. And he wasn't lying then, either. We were given a new world. A world of damp, subterranean caves and eternal darkness. The curse stopped following those who were no longer Junes.

Nihaz speaks the truth, but his words are pure poison, for the truth is different for everyone. And you always hear the truth that you want to hear. It's not too late to come to your senses! Challenge Nihaz and take him down. Otherwise, sooner or later his lies will destroy you more surely than the sharpest blade!"
text

When traveling through the Misty Lands, you probably noticed that they are full of the brainless undead. But where do they come from?

Let me tell you: the Dead City wasn't always dead. The Black Night destroyed it - you also know it as the Cataclysm. One monarch once ruled over this land...

Nihaz will tell you the rest:

"Here in the throne room of the Dead City, I sense the presence of something I can't see...

It's a ghost! The last ruler of the Dead City, as far as I can tell. What does he want?

Oh, so that's it! He was not slain in a fair fight, as befits a king, but fell at the hand of a hired killer. A familiar story... Now he wants another, peaceful death. For this to happen, he requests that we remove the relics that belonged to him in life. We will then resurrect him for a short time and slay him in a proper fight.

Shall we help this long-dead king, or should we leave him to haunt the ruins?"

Of course you decided to help. Although that king had no intention of dying peacefully...

"Aha! Prepare for battle! Something tells me that the ghost wants to go to eternal rest, surrounded by fallen enemies, as befits a true leader!

Can you hear those hushed whispers in the corners of the hall? Those are the ghosts of the Dead City. They have come to pay a tribute of respect to their lord! I don't know if he was a good king or a bad one, but he will die a royal death, he he! To fall by the hand of the great heroes of Sarnaut is an honorable end. What's more, you can expect a truly royal reward, so prepare for battle.  It will be a difficult fight!"

Thanks to you, the king can rest in peace. Your reward is waiting for you...

"The Dead King can finally rest in peace.  The ancient tragedy has come to its proper conclusion. And you receive the armor of the dead king as the winner."
text

You must be interested in Nihaz's Seals and the Keys to them. But this is not the time for that. It's enough that you know they exist and that they are extremely important. Not everyone can handle their power. I'll give you a hint: any of your Great Mages can do it.

But as you understand, the Draconids do not have Great Mages. None of them would drink dragon blood. However, to achieve his goal in the Dead City, the Fiery Father needed someone who could handle the Seals. That someone was Lickflame Tinderbox, the Great Draconid Shaman.

Of course, demons hated him. Still, he's one of the first children of the Fiery Father, the one who could ruin Sarn's plans. That's what doomed Lickflame. And he had no chance of surviving an encounter with you.

Sad, isn't it? But as Nihaz said, what's the point of a Play without a tragedy? Good authors kill off their characters often.
text

So, the Great Dragon... It's ironic that we meet him here... after all, it was here that he once met Ath-Zak. This date went much more peacefully back then. But the Fiery Father's current goals made him reckless.

I must say there is a lot of confusion when it comes to dragons. There are too few of them, so any dragon that is slightly bigger than a horse is called Great. But no, the real Great Dragons are also the Keepers. It's the dozen that guarded Sarn at the dawn of the world. And their descendants like Soliskar the Wise and Agrus the Callous are just... teenagers. They have yet to become Great. If, of course, they are allowed to. Doesn't it surprise you that they aren't here?

But let us get back to the Fiery Father. Oh, he's careful. Otherwise, he wouldn't have survived the massacre carried out by the Junes. But now he's so close to his goal, and it makes him vulnerable. I will quote our immortal classic:

"You know what I hate more than anything? Stupid, petty betrayal.

Take the Great Dragon, for example. I forgave him for failing to defend the prison. Everyone makes mistakes. But his attempt to wage war against me is like a pup trying to pick a fight with a big wolfhound - pointless and stupid. It seems he has forgotten who he's dealing with! I'll have to remind him.

Go with the troop to the Upper City and rid me of this overgrown lizard. He's no longer useful to me."
text

I have a suspicion that of all the enemies of Nihaz, you have the least sympathy for demons. But the Wormfaces are a different matter. Which is unsurprising: you had a chance to meet them back on Gipat, and Ath-Zak's story inspires certain sympathy for this hero.

I will share with you one secret policy of our close friends: while they call themselves the Overmind and maintain constant psionic contact, there are many individualists among them. The Wormfaces are not as united as they appear to be.

And you were about to meet with the leaders of this campaign: Shilonen, Coatl, and Atslan. The Wormface mentors.

One of them was once a great sage and philosopher, the second was a powerful mage, and the third was a most skilled warrior. But their skills did not help them in the fight against Sarn's curse, and then they crawled on their knees to Nihaz and became what they are today. Their long life is also the result of Nihaz's gift. Or another curse? Depends on how you look at it...

Even back then, this trio was spinning a web of intrigues, unaware that the Great Dragon also wanted them dead. Nihaz pitted his enemies against each other, and you helped finish them off.
text

You may have heard this from me before, but demons don't have proper names. They don't even know the meaning of having one. However, the cultists of Sarn, who have ordinary inhabitants of Sarnaut in their ranks, have given them names.

There is an ancient Kanian legend about the mysterious Nav's Kingdom which is the exact opposite of the real world. And its mistress Nav lives there.

We will not be analyzing the eschatology of primitive tribes and wonder if there is something real behind this. Another important thing is that one of Sarn's creatures was named Nav. Why? Well, it's a demon of such psionic power that it can distort reality... Create a copy of reality. And the rules of that reality are established by Nav!

This... Nav is dangerous, smart and even seductive in a way. Her charms will make you fall into her arms. Things look bad, but then a third party intervenes - this time the Wormfaces. They hate Sarn's Curse which destroyed their people. They distracted Nav, wore her out, and you and other heroes finished what they started.
text

It's been a long time since you walked along the path that the God of Darkness suggested. You became his faithful disciples and followers, even though he did not demand worship from you. Here in the Dead City, you have recognized his lies and found the courage to challenge him.

Nihaz was probably surprised. This battle was legendary, but you won.

"Ungrateful scum! ME! I uplifted you! I gave you powers! I gave you knowledge that exists nowhere else in the universe! And this is how you repay me? You should have heeded the old saying about the hand that feeds you! Traitor... I hoped that at least someone in this universe was able to appreciate the beauty of my ideas. I gave you a better life... And this is how you repay me?! That winged worm put you up to this? To betray your daddy? Not good...

You really think that ordinary weapons can kill a god? Hahaha! You were able to destroy my physical body, this husk. Too bad my little girl isn't around... But that’s fine. Presently I might not be in the condition to turn you to ash on the spot, but remember, vermin: I will return. And if I happen to be in a good mood, I'll give you one more chance to serve me. You'd better agree when that happens, or else the tortures that my friend Sarn endured will pale in comparison!

Remember, fool: only the gods or forces equal to gods can destroy gods. And you, parasites, are abusing this power! Patrons... what a joke. It's nothing but another lie. Even your lies are pathetic... There are no Patrons. Or rather, all your mages died in the Cataclysm. They are dead. And the Surges you and your allies use so brazenly - I created them! First I gave some of my power to the dragons, but those brainless lizards wasted it. The power spilled out of them like water from a torn waterskin. Predictably, they were left weak and vulnerable... The Junes took advantage of it, mowing them down. Then I replaced the useless dragons with the Seals: concentrated power that would keep Sarn imprisoned.

If it hadn't been for your Cataclysm, the whole thing might have lasted for quite a while. Luckily for Sarn and unluckily for us, the catastrophe affected the Seals, and part of their power was lost to the Astral. Part of my power! The power of the dragons, the remnants of which were used by your mages, and the power of the Seals, which you believe is the power of your Patrons - all this power came from me! Do you really think you can destroy me with my own weapons?

Frankly, I'm not even offended by your actions. Furthermore, I would have questioned your bravery and ambition if you hadn't challenged me. But I must say you picked the wrong time to interfere. You still can't use the Gates, no matter how hard you try. As for you, we'll meet again!"

And then the Dark God vanished... You need to inform the leaders of the states.
text

Sarn's attempt to escape from his prison. I think I'll let Nihaz speak this time. He is the Director, after all:

"Well then, it's time to deal with Sarn's demons. Our prisoner's starting to get a little restless. Who knows, he might actually be able to break out of his prison. If that happens, I won't be able to rebuild it; I'll just have to smite him. But he's more useful to me in one piece. It's fascinating how with every attempt to free himself, he acquires a new dark stain on his offensively pure soul. He'll never get those stains out, haha...

Here in the Dead City, demons obey the Earth Destroyer - a self-propelled battering ram capable of "destroying the walls of a jail cell" and freeing its creator. Jokes aside, this time Sarn created almost a perfect executor of his plans, a helper who brings only death and destruction. More and more, Sarn reminds me of myself when I was young! I was always trying to create all kinds of different monsters before I learned that brute force always loses to careful calculation.

But brute force might just do the trick in this situation. So, my friend, I need you to hunt down the Earth Destroyer. It's a powerful foe, but if you can put together a good team, you'll defeat it without any trouble."

I should add that Sarn's demons were already on the surface of allods by that time, far from the astral plane. These are not Kirah creatures that died like fish out of water. The Earth Destroyer did not need the Astral - he carried the Astral to you. It's a machine for processing material into primary matter. I'm really glad you managed to bring it down.
text

Have you dealt with the Earth Destroyer? Excellent. I appreciate that. Let my godling friend sit in limbo and think about what he's done, right? Haha!"

Those were the words of the Dark God. But there was also news from the former God of Light...

"As soon as you approach the slowly dissolving shape of the defeated demon, your mind is flooded with visions.

You see Sarn struggling against the darkness that binds his body, radiating pure white light. Every motion causes him to flinch in pain, and his body remains stained by the shadow of darkness. The stains grow with each attempt to escape.

You can see that Nihaz is playing a game with the imprisoned god, a cruel experiment where every attempt at freeing himself brings Sarn closer to his breaking point where he will have no strength left to battle darkness, becoming just like Nihaz. The god of darkness has entertained himself for years, offering Sarn the chance to escape from his prison, but then dashing his hopes at the last moment.

You see a strange structure installed in the throne room of the Dead City, and you can see that it's the Star Gates, Sarn's last hope. If the demons could take the gates, then Sarn would be freed. He could leave this world. But Nihaz once again uses others to fight battles for him - the heroes of this universe who believed in his good intentions.

History repeats itself... Once, the Junes believed Nihaz, and it destroyed them. The same fate awaits both the League and the Empire. The only chance to escape the tragic lot of the Junes is to stop Nihaz before it's too late."
text

During their heyday, the Junes were extremely powerful. Thanks to their considerable talents, they were able to create autonomous mechanisms - golems. This mixture of magic and technology may seem crude to you now, but believe me - even now you have nothing on what the Junes could do.

Golems did all the dirty and hard work for them. In many ways, it was thanks to them that their empire was able to defeat the dragons, because the numerous caves that the Wormfaces now inhabit are shelters of ancient times, dug out by golems for protection against the fire-breathing creatures.

Of course, the Junes also tried to create battle golems. You already know Ram Shaitan, the guardian of the Frontier, but the golems created shortly before the fall were perfect machines of destruction. Ultranis is one of their prototypes, and its power is shocking.

However, as you already know, the golems did not save the Junes from the Curse. Ultranis is strong but not invulnerable. That's why you were able to defeat it.
text

Our world is an amazing place. Sarn was a very inspired creator. Even when building the perfect destroyers of his prison, he created a great variety of creatures...

There is some sad irony in the fact that many of them joined his jailers. I'm talking about dragons and those who serve them. Do you know that the drakes were created by Sarn for the purpose of opposing the winged guardians? But here's another cause for sarcasm - only black drakes, considered by all to be traitors, serve their true creator.

But let's get to the point. At a time when the world was intact, among the creatures that inhabited it were terrestrial dragon-like creatures - salamanders, huge fire-breathing lizards. Now there are very few of them left, but you were going to meet one that has survived to this day. Thunderhead, the Gate Keeper. The "faithful dog" of the Draconids and the Fiery Father, placed here to keep you from going any further.

Do I need to say who came out the winner?
text

So, where were we? Perhaps, while traveling through these islands of Umoir, you have forgotten how it all began...

During the final battle with Tep, Klavdia Kalugina captured his Spark and then disappeared. The leaders of the League and the Empire, concerned about this, sent you after Klavdia.

The trail led you right here, to the League allod Umoir which was controlled by the Great Sorceress Catherina. Umoir is afflicted by a strange disease - the Blight which infects both animals and plants, turning them into monsters. In addition, Catherina is in conflict with adherents of old beliefs, trying to spread faith in the Light.

You managed to find out the following:

First, Klavdia used the power of Tep's Spark to establish her cult and faith in her as a protector. She's trying to gain as much power as possible. Did you really think she was bad? Tsk tsk!

Second, the Old Gods of Umoir really exist, and their power also depends on faith in them.

Third, some incomprehensible threat is approaching, and even the gods fear it.

In the end, you managed to reconcile the adherents of the old and new faith. However, the moment it happened, you were attacked by demons. In addition, the doors of Catherina's tower closed, and her guards began to attack anyone who tried to enter. After you finally managed to get into the tower, an unpleasant surprise awaited you there.

I have to retell the story once again...

"Catherina serves Sarn who created the Blight. There's no doubt about it. I do not care whether is was a conscious decision or not, but that doesn't matter. What matters is that the Eclipse is about to sail off to the heart of the world where Sarn is imprisoned. And I don't think it's a social visit! I'm sure she has keys to the Seals. Maybe not all of them, but even one broken Seal would be enough. My father is far away from this world, so no one would be able to stop the Prisoner. If he breaks free, Sarnaut is doomed!"

Of course, you had to follow her! Follow Catherina!

Maybe not all of them, but even one broken Seal would be enough. My father is far away from this world, so no one would be able to stop the Prisoner. If he breaks free, Sarnaut is doomed!"

Of course, you had to follow her! Follow Catherina!
text

Is it good that the Eclipse is such a big cruiser? If this ship was fast and highly maneuverable, would you have caught up with it? But Catherina likes big... Ahem... Boats!

Of course, the Octulhu delayed you, but you still managed to catch up with the Eclipse. Now it was time to heroically board it. Fortunately, you are a person of reckless courage. A real daredevil!

Perhaps I will quote another hero of this story. The one and only. Anton Turischev, astral scientist and your faithful companion in this adventure! Can't leave him out:

"See, that's the Eclipse over there! It's going to be a good fight.

First, we’ll have to break through the shields of the Eclipse. The enemy crew will try and take out our cannoneers. While the shields are up, the traitor’s ship is completely invulnerable. Once they are down, we can use boarding bridges to get to the deck of the Eclipse. Pray that no one falls into the Astral! Don’t even think of jumping over. The Eclipse’s defense devices will kill you instantly. Use the bridges, there's no other way. Then we might have a chance.

Ready? Let's board it!"

So the fight began. Catherina personally organized a warm welcome. Oh, if this sorceress had been casting spells instead of swearing at you, the outcome would have been completely different! It would've been tragic. But even her obsession with Sarn couldn't change this proud woman. She took your boarding as a personal insult and tried to do everything in her power to keep you from breaking through the shields and getting aboard her ship.

Oh, what a fight... In the end, Catherina spat at you and retired to their chambers. The Eclipse was approaching its destination, and she was certain that her servants would stop you before you could get to her.

But you had to make another choice. Anton Turischev described this as well:

"Phew, we did it!

I’ve never been so scared in my life... I just wanted to jump into the Astral - it would've been a quick and painless death. But we did it! We broke through!

The Eclipse is way too large for us to split. They would easily take us out one by one, so we need to decide how we're going to get to the control room. There are two paths: through the upper deck where we'd run into Catherina’s servants, or through the cargo hold where we’ll have to destroy the reactor. Without it, the Eclipse will no longer be a threat. After that, we’ll deal with Catherina. The decision is up to you!"

If you chose the deck, then a meeting with Ignat Krivov awaited you. If you went through the hold - then it's a date with three goblins.
